title: Correlation Compass — Guided request forensics flow with linked spans
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Users need a fast, guided way to investigate a customer-facing error or latency spike across multiple services and model-serving nodes. Existing console trace views surface raw spans and long timelines, but customers (and support engineers) frequently ask for a narrative entrypoint that: 1) highlights the request's causal path, 2) surfaces where correlated events (logs, model fallbacks, rate-limits) occurred, and 3) exposes the minimal filters to reproduce the observed behavior.

Goal: Design a Correlation Compass — a compact, guided request forensics workspace that stitches correlation IDs, span streams, and event markers into an actionable investigator flow. It should be embeddable in the Console's request detail route and usable as a standalone workspace for incident post-mortems. The design must balance detail for debugging with performance (avoid loading all spans by default) and preserve context for rollouts and cost analysis (per-span token cost visible).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Three-pane layout mockups (compact, default, expanded) are delivered in Figma and annotated.
2) Interaction spec: clicking a correlation marker drills to the precise span and expands related KV cache / model-token metadata.
3) Filter-builder presets implemented as design patterns: Service-only, Model-variant-only, Latency-threshold, Error-code.
4) Performance constraints noted: lazy-load deep-span trees, show sample count and sampling rationale.
5) Accessibility checks: keyboard traversal, semantic labels for spans, color palette meets AA contrast.
6) Handoff checklist with engineering (props, telemetry events) and PM sign-off.
notes: Design intent: make the first interaction a high-level map that summarizes the request's path, then allow progressive disclosure into spans and token-level metadata.
We should display cost estimates per span only when the user toggles 'Show token cost' to avoid noise in normal debugging flows.
Consider a lightweight 'stitch' algorithm to surface correlated events from logs and model tool-calls; engineering has a prototype api (ENG-4120).
